name: Styrenix Performance Materials Ltd (formerly INEOS Styrolution India)
tagline: India's dominant styrenics (ABS/SAN/polystyrene) producer, now Agarwal-family-controlled again post the ISAPL/INEOS exit, mid-way through a capacity-doubling program with margins recovering sharply and valuation still cheap on a trailing basis - a genuine turnaround/rerating case, though a mature commodity-chemical TAM keeps it short of a literal 10x thesis.
business_overview: Styrenix Performance Materials (renamed from INEOS Styrolution India after the global JV exited) manufactures styrenics - ABS, SAN, polystyrene and specialty styrenic polymers - for automotive, appliances, packaging and consumer-durable customers. Following the promoter/ownership realignment (the Agarwal family, via Shiva Styrenix Performance Materials, reacquired control from the erstwhile ISAPL/INEOS structure, releasing all pledged shares by 2024), the company is mid-way through a capacity expansion including a new mass-ABS plant, addressing an import-substitution opportunity as LG Polymers' India ABS capacity shut down, leaving only Styrenix and Supreme Petrochem as the major domestic suppliers against ~130-140k tonnes of imports in a ~275k-tonne market. Seeded 2026-09-13 via untrusted X triage (@rajuidesai, medium conviction).

fundamentals_narrative: A genuine margin-recovery story: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin more than doubled YoY (11.9% -> 26.1%) and PAT roughly 2.5x'd, while revenue growth was more modest (~6.6%) - this is a margin/spread-driven earnings story (styrene-monomer spreads and an import-substitution tailwind) more than a volume story. ROE of ~21% and ROCE of ~16.8% are respectable for a commodity petrochemical producer, and debt is low. On an annualised basis (Q1 FY27 PAT x4 ~ Rs 549 Cr against a Rs 3,488 Cr market cap) the stock screens at roughly 6-7x forward earnings if the quarter's margin holds - cheap if durable, though a single strong quarter after a weak prior year should be read cautiously; commodity spreads can compress as fast as they expanded. Despite the strong print, the stock has reportedly fallen to a fresh 52-week low in recent trading, suggesting the market is not yet crediting the margin recovery as durable.

verdict_headline: Genuine margin-recovery and import-substitution story in Indian styrenics, backed by an active, specific ValuePickr thread and cheap annualised valuation - but a mature commodity-chemical TAM and single-quarter margin data keep this a rerating/turnaround case, not a literal 10x-in-2-3-years thesis. Conviction Medium, thesis_fit 'neither' (four_box score permits a label but growth math doesn't support one).
verdict_reasoning: four_box = 3.0 (tailwind yes - explicit import-substitution/capacity dynamic; tam weak - mature, cyclical commodity petrochemical market; moat weak - dominant domestic scale post LG Polymers exit but still a commodity spread business; valuation yes - ~6-7x annualised Q1 FY27 run-rate). Score permits a 10x/100x label but is not applied: analyst_override true - revenue CAGR of ~11.69% and a margin-driven (not volume-driven) recovery in a mature TAM don't support literal 10x-in-2-3-years math even at a cheap multiple.
